static PyMethodDef rlock_methods[] = {
    {"acquire",      _PyCFunction_CAST(rlock_acquire),
     METH_VARARGS | METH_KEYWORDS, rlock_acquire_doc},
    {"release",      (PyCFunction)rlock_release,
     METH_NOARGS, rlock_release_doc},
    {"_is_owned",     (PyCFunction)rlock_is_owned,
     METH_NOARGS, rlock_is_owned_doc},
    {"_acquire_restore", (PyCFunction)rlock_acquire_restore,
     METH_VARARGS, rlock_acquire_restore_doc},
    {"_release_save", (PyCFunction)rlock_release_save,
     METH_NOARGS, rlock_release_save_doc},
    {"_recursion_count", (PyCFunction)rlock_recursion_count,
     METH_NOARGS, rlock_recursion_count_doc},
    {"__enter__",    _PyCFunction_CAST(rlock_acquire),
     METH_VARARGS | METH_KEYWORDS, rlock_acquire_doc},
    {"__exit__",    (PyCFunction)rlock_release,
     METH_VARARGS, rlock_release_doc},

    {"_at_fork_reinit",    (PyCFunction)rlock__at_fork_reinit,
     METH_NOARGS, NULL},

static PyMemberDef rlock_type_members[] = {
    {"__weaklistoffset__", T_PYSSIZET, offsetof(rlockobject, in_weakreflist), READONLY},
    {NULL},
};

static PyType_Slot rlock_type_slots[] = {
    {Py_tp_dealloc, (destructor)rlock_dealloc},
    {Py_tp_repr, (reprfunc)rlock_repr},
    {Py_tp_methods, rlock_methods},
    {Py_tp_alloc, PyType_GenericAlloc},
    {Py_tp_new, rlock_new},
    {Py_tp_members, rlock_type_members},
    {Py_tp_traverse, rlock_traverse},
    {0, 0},
};

static PyType_Spec rlock_type_spec = {
    .name = "_thread.RLock",
    .basicsize = sizeof(rlockobject),
    .flags = (Py_TPFLAGS_DEFAULT | Py_TPFLAGS_BASETYPE |
              Py_TPFLAGS_HAVE_GC | Py_TPFLAGS_IMMUTABLETYPE),
    .slots = rlock_type_slots,
};

findings: Both complete proposed file Git/SHA256/UTF-8 byte pins independently recomputed and fetched. All ten complete primary provider files independently fetched at both immutable commits and byte-equal to proposal.

The exact native BuiltinFunctionType check precedes object-level metadata reads. CPython methodobject.c reads __name__ from m_ml->ml_name and __self__ from m_self; both getters have null setters. Writable __module__ metadata is not used for this ownership proof.

HASH and RLock are genuine immutable heap types in the pinned C sources. Exact type metaclass, exact-string raw namespace keys, immutable flag, identity-only object base/MRO, fixed native descriptor owner/name checks reject ordinary Python classes, subclasses, copied foreign descriptors and opaque metadata without invoking them.

Native sha256 dispatch passes the fixed algorithm to py_evp_fromname and creates the module-state EVPtype. This establishes the intended native constructor only under independently admitted exact bytes and trusted installed OpenSSL/native binary preconditions.

Raw module/class namespace iteration precedes string dictionary lookups. Text comparison requires exact str; bases and MRO comparisons use identity. No hash/lock construction, lock acquisition, digest/update, weakref count or isfinite calculation occurs in this predicate.

All 26 prospective cases are source-derived from nine definitions: 1 canonical, 8 aliases, 5 immutable method owners, 4 opaque module-key collisions, 2 opaque class-key collisions, 3 unknown-type controls, 1 missing backend, 1 wrong algorithm, 1 unsupported runtime. Unsupported-version skip is explicit; no actual collection or result is claimed.
limits: Caller must prove this guard and its captured inspection anchors/globals/bootstrap, actual application aliases, exact input shapes, newly native-created HASH provenance and exact owned RLock instance/slot. The source guard cannot authenticate its own mutable globals.

Native function/type identity is not a proof of all window effects. RLock acquire_timed may release the GIL and call _PyEval_MakePendingCalls following an interrupted wait. Large hash initialization/update can release the GIL. Caller signal/window/reentrancy/concurrency admission remains necessary.

math.isfinite's generated conversion admits arbitrary __float__/__index__ for general objects; caller exact primitive input restriction remains necessary. Exact bytes likewise avoids arbitrary buffer providers.

No arbitrary extension-forged native types, ctypes/native-memory tampering, complete heap guarantee, OpenSSL configuration attestation, Python parsing/formatting/type checking/import, tests, performance, workload, source commit, refs or workflow launch.
